record.what_it_does: Lark is an all-in-one workplace/collaboration suite (chat, calendar, docs, base, approvals) whose Open Platform exposes REST server APIs, events, and an official MCP server for building bots and integrations.
record.auth_notes: Server calls use three token types: tenant_access_token (app acting as itself/tenant, obtained via app_id+app_secret, no user consent), app_access_token, and user_access_token (obtained via a standard OAuth2 authorization-code flow at /open-apis/authen/v2/oauth/token, used when acting on behalf of a user). All tokens are sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. The tenant_access_token flow is effectively a client-credentials/API-key-like exchange rather than third-party OAuth.
record.access_notes: An individual developer can immediately create a free-trial Lark organization, register a 'Custom App' in the Developer Console, and get an App ID/Secret with no cost and no Lark review ('do not require review by the Lark team and can be used once approved by the enterprise tenant administrator') — sufficient for self-serve testing since the trial creator is their own tenant admin. However, Custom Apps are hard-restricted to a single tenant ('Custom apps are limited to development, review, and usage within a single tenant... No custom apps can be used by other organizations'). Building a real multi-user/multi-tenant agent toolkit requires becoming a 'Store App', which requires passing ISV verification and a 'strict review by the official Lark operation' before other tenants can install/authorize it — this is the approval-gated path relevant to an agent toolkit.
record.main_blocker: Cross-tenant (multi-customer) distribution requires ISV verification and Lark's official Store App listing review; single-tenant Custom Apps work self-serve but can't serve other orgs.
